title: MCP Transports: stdio and Stateless Streamable HTTP
service: streamhttp: a stateless MCP 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP endpoint with a shared SQLite draft store, request-scoped SSE and a layered client-side reader

parts.lesson_anchor: Required HTTP metadata headers (names case-insensitive, exact decoded values, Mcp-Name mirrors params.uri for resources/read, Exercise 3); code/main.py reject_duplicate_routing_headers and code/tests/test_main.py conflicting duplicate name headers; the Content-Length rules in code/tests/test_main.py
planted_bugs: Headers.get_all compares header names exactly, so the lowercase names of an HTTP/2 hop are not found; the error surfaces one call up as FramingError: Content-Length is required

_expect refuses only an empty values list and then compares its first value, so repeated routing headers are accepted when the first mirrors the body, even when another parser would choose a conflicting second value
body_name always mirrors params.name, so a resources/read whose Mcp-Name mirrors params.uri is rejected
read_body accumulates the body with bytes +=, which copies everything read so far on every chunk, O(n^2)
parts.timing_assert: a 12 MiB body read in 4 KiB pieces under 0.1 s (the bytes += version takes 1.1-1.5 s on a quiet machine and up to about 3.5 s under heavy load; bytearray takes 2-3 ms, 4-6 ms under load)
parts.overfix_guard: the strict Content-Length rules survive the faster read: a missing, conflicting, signed, zero, over-limit or non-ASCII-digit length and a Content-Length beside a lowercase transfer-encoding are refused before any read; a short body is refused; exactly Content-Length bytes are consumed and the rest stays in the stream. Lowercasing the values along with the names, stripping values, and lowercasing only one side of the comparison are caught too. Every mirrored routing header must occur once even when values agree or header-name casing differs; a single mixed-case header and an exactly decoded Base64 value still pass. Exact value comparison and sentinel decoding are supplied behavior, guarded against case folding or stripping.
parts.deviation: The suggested timing case was 1 MB read 1 KB at a time. On this machine the quadratic copy of 1 MiB takes about 10 ms against 0.3 ms for the fix, too close for an 8x margin on both sides; the gap grows with the body size, not the read size, so the test reads 12 MiB in 4 KiB pieces with limit=16 MiB. The planted line is body += chunk on bytes, the same copy as body = body + chunk. Base64 sentinel decoding is working code inside the mirrored-header check, where the comparison happens; Part 1 covers it through Exercise 3, and Part 3 checks its effect at the HTTP layer.

parts.lesson_anchor: Explicit application state: the five-step replica failure; a server-minted opaque handle bound to principal and tenant, unguessable, expiring, with concurrency control; durable state in a shared store
parts.exactness: a draft written through one replica's connection loads through another's as an identical Draft: text with CRLF, trailing spaces and a tab, U+2028 and an emoji, an integer version, and expires_at_ms as integer milliseconds from the injected clock

parts.deviation: Expiry is fixed at creation and save does not extend it. The race between two replicas that read the version and then update unconditionally cannot be interleaved deterministically in a single-threaded test, so it is an interviewer follow-up.

parts.lesson_anchor: POST-only means POST-only (405, Mcp-Session-Id and Last-Event-ID ignored); Origin validation (present and not allowed is 403, absent passes, exact matching); Required HTTP metadata headers (-32020 before -32022 with exact data, 404 with a -32601 body); 202 for an accepted notification; HTTP dual-era compatibility

parts.integration: two StreamableServer replicas share one SQLite file: replica 1 mints a draft handle, a fresh POST to replica 2 saves through it, and another principal gets a tool error; a Base64 Mcp-Name passes and malformed, raw non-ASCII or missing ones are -32020
clarifying_questions: HTTP status for other JSON-RPC errors
parts.deviation: Sentinel decoding stays in Part 1's code, so this part checks it only at the HTTP layer. The lesson code's 415 and 406 checks are left out because the lesson text does not define them. A path other than /mcp (a 404 without a JSON-RPC body) and PUT (405) are added so that both kinds of 404 and POST-only are exercised.

parts.lesson_anchor: Request-scoped SSE: notifications related to the request, then the final response, then the stream closes; no SSE event ids; closing the response stream cancels the request; SSE comments as keepalives
parts.wire_format: text/event-stream bytes: each event is one line, a ':' comment or a single 'data: ' line of compact JSON, followed by a blank line, decided by the test's strict parser

parts.deviation: Keepalives come from Heartbeat steps that the tool yields rather than from a timer, which keeps the test deterministic and the part on framing; the timer version and its asyncio.wait_for cancellation pitfall are a follow-up, and timing and backpressure belong to lesson 29. This lesson does not define the progress fields, so the notification uses the params of lesson 29's code (progressToken, progress, optional total and message) and the token is passed in.

parts.lesson_anchor: Streamable HTTP responses: application/json with one response, or text/event-stream with related notifications and then the final response; no server requests on the stream (sampling, elicitation and roots use MRTR); a stream that breaks before its final response loses the request

parts.integration: the reader decodes what Part 4's stream_tool_call writes
parts.deviation: The lesson has no tree or DAG, so Part 5 is the client's three nested framings, HTTP Content-Type, SSE events and JSON-RPC messages, as the chapter plan assigns. Only LF and CRLF line ends are required; a lone CR is a follow-up.
